title: Mirabel and the Ledger
premise: Emrys Ashgrove, the unassuming archivist of St. Vellum's Cathedral, has spent years quietly untangling deaths the police misfiled as accidents, keeping a private ledger of evidence no one asked for. When a drowned chorister is found wearing clothes stolen from Emrys's own closet, the killer makes it unmistakably personal: someone has read Emrys's ledger and is staging murders from its pages. As the statute of limitations on an old, buried death ticks down, Emrys must ally with a skeptical detective and confront the truth that their late mentor, the previous archivist, was both their teacher and the origin of every case in the ledger. In the end, Emrys traps the killer—the mentor's own child, avenging a death the ledger was secretly built to hide—by choosing truth over loyalty, publishing the archive and surrendering their invisibility forever.
about_author: Elodie Halloran is a former parish records clerk from the Welsh marches who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of births, debts, and quiet scandals before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A routine inventory of the cathedral crypt reveals the inner vault sealed with a lock only the dead archivist could open. Emrys catalogs the anomaly in their private ledger, establishing their habit of recording what others overlook. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Chorister Tomas Pell is found drowned in the baptistry, dressed in garments lifted from Emrys's own closet. Detective Sergeant Idris Vance arrives and, to Emrys's horror, recognizes details only the ledger contains. Emotional beat: exposure—the invisible witness suddenly at the center.

chapters.title: What the Police Called Accidents
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, flashback-woven. Under questioning, Emrys conceals three prior 'accidents' they solved privately: the bell-ringer, the gardener, the visiting scholar. Each chapter of memory shows how the ledger grew. Emotional beat: guilt over silence compounding into fear.

chapters.title: Vance Reads the File
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. The detective reconstructs the old cases from police files and notices they mirror Emrys's timeline exactly. He suspects Emrys either committed all four deaths or predicted them. Emotional beat: wary mutual suspicion sharpening into reluctant respect.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Margins
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Searching the late Archivist Corwin Ashgrove's papers, Emrys finds marginal annotations in a second hand—someone else has studied these documents recently. A pressed lily, Corwin's favorite flower, marks the page. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Choir of Suspects
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Emrys and Vance interview the cathedral staff: the verger with gambling debts, the organist who resented Tomas, the dean hiding financial irregularities. Everyone lies about something small. Emotional beat: the claustrophobia of a community where everyone keeps ledgers of their own.

chapters.title: The Statute
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Legal research reveals that the oldest death in the ledger—the one that started everything, twenty years ago—expires from prosecution in eleven days. Whoever killed Tomas is racing a clock Emrys didn't know existed. Emotional beat: urgency replacing caution.

chapters.title: Stolen From My Closet
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Forensics confirms the clothes were taken during the funeral for Corwin himself—meaning the killer stood among the mourners, watching Emrys grieve. Emrys replays every face from that day. Emotional beat: violation; home is no longer safe.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. Vance discovers Corwin kept his own ledger—a darker one—recording not solutions but concealments, including a death he helped bury two decades ago. He confronts Emrys with it. Emotional beat: betrayal; the mentor's pedestal cracks.

chapters.title: What Corwin Buried
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Deciphering Corwin's coded entries, Emrys learns the original victim: a young woman named Serafin Vale, whose death was staged as a runaway's disappearance. The statute clock belongs to her case. Emotional beat: horror that the ledger's foundation is a cover-up.

chapters.title: The Vale Family
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Emrys and Vance trace Serafin's surviving family and find her brother, Rhys Vale, now a conservator who restored the cathedral's manuscripts—including, briefly, Corwin's private papers. Emotional beat: the hunter's outline begins to take shape.

chapters.title: An Invitation in Ash
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A fourth entry appears in Emrys's own ledger, written in handwriting mimicking theirs: a date, a time, the crypt. The killer is corresponding through the book itself. Emotional beat: terror fused with a strange, terrible intimacy.

chapters.title: Trap or Be Trapped
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. Vance proposes using the invitation to stage an arrest, but Emrys realizes the killer anticipates police procedure because they've studied the same files. They must design a trap outside the file's logic. Emotional beat: partnership solidifying into trust.

chapters.title: The Verger Confesses
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The debt-ridden verger breaks down and admits he was paid to leave the crypt door unlocked on the night Tomas died—but not by whom. The payment came in old banknotes, pre-2001 issue. Emotional beat: pity entangled with manipulation; even confessions are currency.

chapters.title: Rhys Vale's Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Rhys tells them about Serafin: her scholarship, her discovery of financial fraud in the cathedral restoration fund, her last meeting with Corwin. He denies killing anyone—but his alibi for Tomas's death is a lie. Emotional beat: sympathy for a grieving man who may still be guilty.

chapters.title: The Night Before Expiry
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. With one day left on the statute, Emrys rereads the entire ledger and finds what they missed: the marginal annotations aren't Rhys's hand—they're Corwin's, written before his death. Corwin knew he was being watched, and left a final cipher. Emotional beat: the mentor reaching across death to finish the lesson.

chapters.title: Corwin's Last Cipher
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The cipher decodes to a location: Serafin's remains, hidden beneath the locked inner vault, along with Corwin's full confession—he caused her death in a panic and spent his life atoning by training Emrys to solve what he couldn't confess. Emotional beat: devastating inheritance; the truth is the bequest.

chapters.title: Into the Vault
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Emrys opens the inner vault at last and finds Serafin's remains—and Rhys waiting, holding the stolen clothes, weeping. He followed his sister's trail for twenty years and used Emrys's methods because they were Corwin's methods. But he swears Tomas's death wasn't his. Emotional beat: confrontation as tragedy, not triumph.

chapters.title: The Fifth Accident
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Reexamining Tomas's death with fresh eyes, Emrys realizes the staging was too perfect—deliberately drawing police toward Rhys. The real killer needed the statute to expire with Serafin's case unsolved: the dean, whose fraud Serafin discovered, and whose career Corwin's silence protected. Emotional beat: clarity arriving cold and complete.

chapters.title: Ledger Against Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Emrys and Vance lay a false trail through the ledger itself, feeding the dean a fabricated entry suggesting Corwin hid evidence in the vault. The dean comes at night to destroy it—and finds Emrys, Vance, and a recording device instead. Emotional beat: the quiet power of the underestimated turning fully upon the powerful.

chapters.title: The Statute Expires
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The dean confesses to Serafin's murder and Tomas's, believing the old crime untouchable—but Corwin's dated confession, legally witnessed and sealed with the cathedral notary, revives the case within the window. Justice arrives hours inside the deadline. Emotional beat: catharsis; the ledger's long patience rewarded.

chapters.title: Mirabel's Door
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, epilogue. Emrys donates the full archive—Corwin's crimes included—to the county records office, ending a lifetime of invisible vigilance, and unlocks the crypt permanently as a memorial to Serafin Vale. Vance asks what they'll do now. Emrys answers: 'Someone has to keep the ledger.' Emotional beat: peace earned through chosen truth; identity finally claimed.
